newSources.whatItSupports: Origin of Normal Accidents Theory: in systems with interactive complexity and tight coupling, serious accidents are inevitable ('normal').

newSources.title: The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons
newSources.whatItSupports: Applies normal-accidents theory to US nuclear command and control, documenting Cold War near-accidents (Lewis, 14 also cites it).

newSources.title: International Norm Dynamics and Political Change
newSources.whatItSupports: Defines the 'norm cascade' stage of the norm life cycle. It is theory only, with no TPNW data, so pair it with PAX/ICAN, 22 and 23.

summary: Checked all 171 PRO items (41 changed, 130 new) plus the 3 new source cards: 105 edits (15 critical, 51 major, 39 minor) and 7 new sources. Reintroduced errors fixed: Rosatom described as a 'binding legal mandate' or legal ban (should be a legal and moral argument); 14% applied to European NATO; SIPRI totals labeled 'conventional'; Harvard's umbrella condition dropped; van Hooft, Lewis, Shlapak and Davis overstated; 'obsolete' B61s; 38% of 250,000 missing 'as of 2016'. New errors fixed: ICRC and Xia et al. misattributed for water, milk and 'fridge' contamination (CDC says refrigerated and sealed food is SAFE); invented B61 'personal launch codes' (Sweeney: US presidential release authorization); UN veto is Art. 27, not 23; national enforcement is TPNW Art. 5, not 1(1)(e); Article 5 is not 'automatic'; EU has passed energy sanctions (it is the nuclear sector that is unsanctioned); 1,700 US warheads include bombers; CWC and BWC were joined by the superpowers. Brennan & Panetta card: fake title; the 'NATO allies anxiety' line was European Pravda narration, not Brennan; the 'strongmen' quote was not found; replaced with Panetta's confirmed One Decision Article 5 quote and Brennan's confirmed Times Radio quote. No source has 'Trump does not have NATO's back' verbatim. Side note: Sweeney's report does cite a RAND excursion with 5,000 deaths per base at Aviano and Ramstein, so earlier rounds' 'no source has it' was wrong. No edit needed here.
